nodes.summary: For every natural number $r$, the formal power series $\sum_{n \ge 0} \binom{n+r}{r} t^n$ with integer coefficients satisfies $\left(\sum_{n \ge 0} \binom{n+r}{r} t^n\right)(1-t)^{r+1} = 1$ in $\mathbb{Z}[[t]]$, that is, $\sum_{n \ge 0} \binom{n+r}{r} t^n = 1/(1-t)^{r+1}$.
nodes.title: Generating function of shifted binomial coefficients

nodes.summary: The hyper-Fibonacci numbers $F^{(1)}_n$ of order $1$ satisfy $F^{(1)}_0 = 0$, $F^{(1)}_1 = 1$, $F^{(1)}_2 = 2$ and $F^{(1)}_3 = 4$.
nodes.title: Small values of the hyper-Fibonacci numbers of order one

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $r$ and $n$, the hyper-Fibonacci numbers $F^{(r)}_n$ satisfy $F^{(r+1)}_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} F^{(r)}_k$.
nodes.title: Hyper-Fibonacci numbers as partial sums

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the hyper-Fibonacci number $F^{(0)}_n$ equals the $n$-th Fibonacci number $F_n$ (with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$).
nodes.title: Hyper-Fibonacci numbers of order zero

nodes.summary: The hyper-Fibonacci numbers $F^{(r)}_n$, for natural numbers $r$ and $n$, are the natural numbers defined by $F^{(0)}_n = F_n$, the $n$-th Fibonacci number (with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$), and $F^{(r+1)}_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} F^{(r)}_k$.
nodes.title: Hyper-Fibonacci numbers

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $r$ and $n \ge 1$, the hyper-Leonardo numbers $\mathrm{Le}^{(r)}_n$ satisfy $2 \mathrm{Le}^{(r)}_n \le \mathrm{Le}^{(r)}_{n-1} + \mathrm{Le}^{(r)}_{n+1}$.
nodes.title: Convexity of the hyper-Leonardo numbers

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $r$ and $n$, the hyper-Leonardo number $\mathrm{Le}^{(r)}_n$ and the hyper-Fibonacci number $F^{(r)}_{n+1}$ satisfy $\mathrm{Le}^{(r)}_n = 2F^{(r)}_{n+1} - \binom{n+r}{r}$ as integers.
nodes.title: Hyper-Leonardo numbers in terms of hyper-Fibonacci numbers

nodes.summary: For every natural number $r$, the formal power series $\sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{Le}^{(r)}_n t^n$ of the hyper-Leonardo numbers of order $r$ satisfies $\left(\sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{Le}^{(r)}_n t^n\right)(1-2t+t^3)(1-t)^r = 1-t+t^2$ in $\mathbb{Z}[[t]]$, that is, $\sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{Le}^{(r)}_n t^n = \frac{1-t+t^2}{(1-2t+t^3)(1-t)^r}$.
nodes.title: Generating function of the hyper-Leonardo numbers

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $r \ge 1$ and $n \ge 2$, the hyper-Leonardo numbers $Le^{(r)}_n$ of order $r$ satisfy $Le^{(r)}_{n-1} Le^{(r)}_{n+1} \le (Le^{(r)}_n)^2$.
nodes.title: Eventual log-concavity of the hyper-Leonardo numbers of positive order

nodes.summary: The hyper-Leonardo numbers $\mathrm{Le}^{(r)}_n$ satisfy $\left(\mathrm{Le}^{(1)}_1\right)^2 \le \mathrm{Le}^{(1)}_0 \mathrm{Le}^{(1)}_2$, and for every natural number $r \ge 2$ they satisfy $\mathrm{Le}^{(r)}_0 \mathrm{Le}^{(r)}_2 \le \left(\mathrm{Le}^{(r)}_1\right)^2$.
nodes.title: Log-convexity and log-concavity of the hyper-Leonardo numbers at index one

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $r \ge 1$ and $n \ge 1$, the hyper-Leonardo numbers $Le^{(r)}_n$ satisfy $Le^{(r)}_{n-1} Le^{(r)}_{n+1} - (Le^{(r)}_n)^2 = Le^{(r)}_n Le^{(r-1)}_{n+1} - Le^{(r-1)}_n Le^{(r)}_{n+1}$.
nodes.title: Cassini-type identity for hyper-Leonardo numbers

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 2$, the hyper-Leonardo numbers $Le^{(1)}_n$ of order $1$ satisfy $Le^{(1)}_{n-1} Le^{(1)}_{n+1} \le (Le^{(1)}_n)^2$.
nodes.title: Eventual log-concavity of the hyper-Leonardo numbers of order one

nodes.summary: The hyper-Leonardo numbers $Le^{(1)}_n$ of order $1$ satisfy $Le^{(1)}_0 = 1$, $Le^{(1)}_1 = 2$, $Le^{(1)}_2 = 5$ and $Le^{(1)}_3 = 10$.
nodes.title: First hyper-Leonardo numbers of order one

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the hyper-Leonardo numbers $Le^{(1)}_n$ of order $1$ satisfy $Le^{(1)}_{n+1} = Le^{(1)}_n + L_{1,n+1}$, where $L_{1,n}$ is the generalized Leonardo number with $k = 1$, that is, the Leonardo number $Le_n$.
nodes.title: Consecutive hyper-Leonardo numbers of order one

nodes.summary: In the ring $\mathbb{Z}[[t]]$ of formal power series, the hyper-Leonardo numbers $Le^{(r)}_n$ satisfy $\left(\sum_{n \ge 0} Le^{(1)}_n t^n\right)(1 - 2t + t^3)(1 - t) = 1 - t + t^2$ and $\left(\sum_{n \ge 0} Le^{(2)}_n t^n\right)(1 - 2t + t^3)(1 - t)^2 = 1 - t + t^2$.
nodes.title: Generating functions of the hyper-Leonardo numbers of orders one and two

nodes.summary: The hyper-Leonardo numbers $Le^{(r)}_n$ satisfy $Le^{(0)}_0 = Le^{(0)}_1 = 1$, $Le^{(1)}_0 = 1$, $Le^{(1)}_1 = 2$, $Le^{(2)}_0 = 1$ and $Le^{(2)}_1 = 3$, and for every natural number $n \ge 2$,
nodes.title: Recurrences for the hyper-Leonardo numbers of orders zero, one and two

nodes.summary: For every natural number $r$, the hyper-Leonardo numbers $Le^{(r)}_n$ of order $r$ satisfy $Le^{(r)}_0 = 1$, $Le^{(r)}_1 = r + 1$ and, for every natural number $n \ge 2$, $Le^{(r)}_n = r + Le^{(r)}_{n-1} + Le^{(r)}_{n-2} + \binom{n+r-2}{r} + \sum_{j=1}^{r-1} j \binom{n+r-2-j}{r-j}$.
nodes.title: Recurrence for the hyper-Leonardo numbers

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $r \ge 1$ and $n \ge 1$, the hyper-Leonardo numbers $Le^{(r)}_n$ satisfy $Le^{(r)}_n = Le^{(r)}_{n-1} + Le^{(r-1)}_n$.
nodes.title: Recurrence across consecutive orders of hyper-Leonardo numbers

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $r$ and $n$, the hyper-Leonardo numbers $Le^{(r)}_n$ satisfy $Le^{(r+1)}_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} Le^{(r)}_k$.
nodes.title: Hyper-Leonardo numbers as partial sums

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the hyper-Leonardo number $Le^{(0)}_n$ equals the Leonardo number $L_{1,n}$, the generalized Leonardo number with $k = 1$, given by $L_{1,0} = L_{1,1} = 1$ and $L_{1,n+2} = L_{1,n+1} + L_{1,n} + 1$.
nodes.title: Hyper-Leonardo numbers of order zero

nodes.summary: Let $Le_n$ be the Leonardo numbers, defined by $Le_0 = Le_1 = 1$ and $Le_{n+2} = Le_{n+1} + Le_n + 1$. The hyper-Leonardo numbers are the integers $Le^{(r)}_n$, for $r, n \ge 0$, defined by $Le^{(0)}_n = Le_n$ and $Le^{(r+1)}_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} Le^{(r)}_k$.
nodes.title: Hyper-Leonardo numbers

nodes.summary: Let $Le_n$ be the Leonardo numbers ($Le_0 = Le_1 = 1$ and $Le_{n+2} = Le_{n+1} + Le_n + 1$), and let $L(t) = \sum_{n \ge 0} Le_n t^n$ in the ring $\mathbb{Z}[[t]]$ of formal power series. Then $L(t)(1 - 2t + t^3) = 1 - t + t^2$ and $L(t)(1 - t - t^2)(1 - t) = 2(1 - t) - (1 - t - t^2)$.
nodes.title: Generating function of the Leonardo numbers

nodes.summary: Let $Le_n$ be the Leonardo numbers ($Le_0 = Le_1 = 1$ and $Le_{n+2} = Le_{n+1} + Le_n + 1$). Then $Le_3^2 \le Le_2 Le_4$ and $\frac{Le_2}{2!} \cdot \frac{Le_4}{4!} \le \left(\frac{Le_3}{3!}\right)^2$, the second inequality in the real numbers. That is, $(Le_n)$ satisfies the log-convexity inequality at $n = 3$ and $(Le_n / n!)$ satisfies the log-concavity inequality at $n = 3$.
nodes.title: Leonardo numbers are log-balanced at index three

nodes.summary: Let $Le_n$ be the Leonardo numbers ($Le_0 = Le_1 = 1$ and $Le_{n+2} = Le_{n+1} + Le_n + 1$). Then $Le_n^2 \le Le_{n-1} Le_{n+1}$ for $n = 1$ and $n = 3$, $Le_5^2 = Le_4 Le_6$, and $Le_{n-1} Le_{n+1} \le Le_n^2$ for $n = 2$, $n = 4$ and every $n \ge 6$.
nodes.title: Log-convexity and log-concavity of the Leonardo numbers

nodes.summary: Let $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ and $(y_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be sequences of positive real numbers that are log-concave, that is, $x_{j-1} x_{j+1} \le x_j^2$ and $y_{j-1} y_{j+1} \le y_j^2$ for every $j \ge 1$. Let $z_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} x_k y_{n-k}$ be their convolution. Then $z_{j-1} z_{j+1} \le z_j^2$ for every $j \ge 1$.
nodes.title: The convolution of log-concave sequences is log-concave

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
